questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a building energy model?
options: To predict energy use under design or operating assumptions

questions.prompt: Which input most directly drives the heating and cooling loads in a model?
options: The weather data for the site

questions.prompt: Select all properties that affect conductive heat transfer through a wall.
options: The colour of the interior furniture
The surface area of the wall

questions.prompt: A variable air volume (VAV) system varies:
options: The air volume delivered to each zone

questions.prompt: Occupancy and lighting schedules in a model should be based on:
options: The realistic expected use of the space
One constant value for every hour

questions.prompt: Calibrating a model against metered data is done to:
options: Bring the model's results in line with observed consumption within an accepted tolerance
Remove the need for utility bills

questions.prompt: Which of these are typical outputs of an energy model used for compliance? Select all that apply.
options: Annual energy use by end use

questions.prompt: Energy use intensity (EUI) is usually expressed as:
options: Energy per unit of floor area per year

questions.prompt: Setting back the temperature setpoint during unoccupied hours generally:

options: Dimming or switching off electric lighting when there is enough daylight
